claims.text: The OBIE v3.1 importer (src/cma/importers/openbanking.py) writes the golden statements byte for byte: per-line balances across two pages, with a pending line left out and counted, a repeated page transaction kept once, and transactions booked at the same moment ordered so the chain holds; and the same statement from a supplied statement balance at four dates. cma case import --format openbanking keeps that statement in the case, reports pending and repeated counts, logs them, and leaves the case unchanged on a second import.

Refusal fixtures: no per-line balance and no statement balance (names --statement-balance AMOUNT --at DATE), a broken balance chain (names the line), equal timestamps no order chains (names the first break), a statement balance that disagrees with per-line balances, a non-GBP booked line or balance (account refused, never converted), a repeated id with different content (names both lines), only pending lines, a malformed status/id/amount/indicator/date/future date/limit amount, two accounts in one file, non-JSON, non-OBIE shape, bad UTF-8 and a duplicate JSON key are each refused naming a line of the file, quoting no cell (a sentinel in descriptions never appears) and writing nothing.
The full suite, the contracts tier and ruff pass with the change.
claims.proof_cmd: python -m pytest -q; python -m pytest -q -m contracts; ruff check src tests

notes: Committed as a92cec2 on bridgie-task/statement-review/T29. Choices the design leaves open: (1) The design's failure-modes row says a non-GBP account or line refuses the account, so any booked line or balance in another currency refuses the file; pending lines are left out whatever their currency. (2) --statement-balance is the closing balance at the end of --at, which must lie from the day before the first booked line to the last; with per-line balances present both must agree. (3) Only booked balance types (ClosingBooked, InterimBooked, OpeningBooked, PreviouslyClosedBooked, or none given) are read as per-line balances; an available or expected balance is ignored. (4) A line's date is the booking date as the bank wrote it (its own offset), ordered within the date by the UTC moment; lines at one moment are ordered by a bounded search for the order their balances chain in. (5) Refusals name the line of the JSON file on which a transaction's object starts (a position-tracking JSON scanner), as the importer contract asks. (6) The import log entry for openbanking gains additive pending and repeated counts; csv and monzo entries are unchanged. No standalone `cma import openbanking` command was added; the task asks for cma case import.
